extracted.subtask_description: Advice for authors building science-fiction worlds, especially when centering a story on one speculative technology and choosing a level of scientific plausibility (soft sci-fi).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a single focal technology
rubrics_metrics.description: If I had to pick one technology, artificial wormholes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select one technology to anchor the story (here: generating a stable portal from one side of the galaxy to the other). Using a clear focal device helps shape plot and world details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a soft sci‑fi plausibility balance
rubrics_metrics.description: It's more soft sci-fi, but the science used within the book is achievable in some aspects and still theoretical in others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend achievable science with theoretical or speculative elements so the story feels plausible without being constrained by current technical limits; decide which parts you treat as established vs. speculative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use scientific 'what‑if' grounded in current gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: Since quantum theory and quantum physics are so vast and we barely understand it, having that bit of 'what-if' is nice for a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage genuine gaps or mysteries in real science (e.g., quantum phenomena) as credible hooks for speculative technologies; this preserves reader suspension of disbelief while enabling imaginative devices.
